Source: A 41-year-old man presents to his primary care provider after seeing bright red blood in the toilet bowl after his last 2 bowel movements.
The patient denies abdominal pain or any changes in his stool habits.
He notes a weight loss of 8 pounds in the last 2 months with no changes in his diet or exercise habits.
He reports that he also noticed some blood mixed with his stool.
His medical history is significant for an episode of pancreatitis 2 years ago for which he was hospitalized for several days.
He has no family history of colon cancer.
He drinks 2-3 beers on the weekend and he has never smoked.
Bowel sounds are present, and there is no hepatomegaly.
On physical exam, his abdomen is soft and non-tender to palpation.
His temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 135/78 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 14/min.
